Related mechanisms

discrete-learning reaches the same goal differently: every move is legal by construction. carrier-credit ran on the same learner and panels but changed where credit goes, not which moves are legal. rank-margin supplies the descent target in its integer form. spin-weights is the source of the quarter-step code set. ternary-xor is another multiplier-free weight alphabet with the same export question.

Live geometric carrier credit

Status: PARKED. The forms that were run either failed or broke a project rule. Three fixed-length runs fell from 437 of 512 correct replies on the development panel (a score that was itself recorded as panel fitting: 0 of 128 on fresh rows) to 0 of 512, the September pilots failed, and the sampled-choice credit used a softmax, which the rules ban (unified integration record). One part of the idea survives: a single shared token table, now live in discrete learning.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

When a model reads a memory and then writes an answer, the lesson from a mistake should reach the pieces that actually carried the information, not only the last few scoring numbers. This idea pushes the error signal back through those carriers: the geometric objects that hold the read, and the prototypes the answer is chosen from. A later version also ties input, memory and output to one shared table of vectors. The runs so far have not shown a benefit. The arm with carrier credit and the arms without it all lost every answer the starting model had right, so the runs cannot blame the credit rule or clear it.

What it replaces in a transformer

Backpropagation's job of blame assignment. In a transformer, the error flows back through every layer by the chain rule. Here the path is a chain of hard choices (which memory, which key, which answer) and geometric carriers, so the credit has to be designed rather than inherited.

Where the error signal lands: the frozen-carrier fit changes only the final coefficients, while the unified fit also moves the carriers and prototypes.

How it works

September form: cost-to-go credit (definition). The addressed-attention model samples four hard trajectories, each a chain of decisions (read, key, emit). The old estimator credited every parameter event with the loss of the whole trajectory. The new one credits an event with the cost that follows it, measured from its next cross-entropy boundary, minus a baseline taken from the other three trajectories. Schematically, for decision \(t\) of trajectory \(i\),

\[\hat g^{(i)}_t=\Big(G^{(i)}_t-\bar G^{(-i)}_t\Big)\,s^{(i)}_t,\qquad G^{(i)}_t=\sum_{u\ge t}c^{(i)}_u,\]

with \(c\) the per-boundary cost and \(s\) the recorded score of the parameter event (the exact normalisation is in the source).

October form: unified credit (definition). The saved native model (called saved437) scores relations between H4 elements (the 120 vertices of the 600-cell, a four-dimensional shape) and Generate prototypes. The unified fit computes independent conditional utilities over all 120 H4 elements. It restores the saved fractional masters, whose served form is quarter-step codes \(q/4\) with \(q\in\{-7,\dots,7\}\). It then fits the context carriers, the prototypes and the coefficients together on the pooled-ranking plus end-of-reply objective. A lane reads at most 120 encountered prototypes.

Whole-path design (hypothesis). Extend credit to compiler spans, exact store writes, E8 root choices and consumed donors through an explicit graph of hard decisions. Exact token, occurrence and version identity stay separate from the geometric summaries.

Shared writer (definition). One learned vector table encodes the input token, ranks the output and carries the compiler/store/emitter channel. Tokens get a product cell from the root numbers of their first and last 8-dimensional block, and a target omitted from the shortlist still receives score credit.

Rule check. The sampled-choice credit used by the whole-path producer uses softmax, so it is blocked by D23, and the pooled-ranking loss used softplus. The shared-writer margin form and the integer writer are compliant. No dense matrix multiplication is needed (D30): the finite factors use table reads and quarter-step sums, and 31 vendor-boundary controls passed for the writer. The served M2 form is already integer (D11), but the export gap of the unified form was never measured, and every position still scores all 4,096 answer choices, so per-token access is not sparse. D37 allows a float re-registration with a fresh review, an owner release, a scanned module and a reported export gap.

Exact addressed memory

Status: PARKED. Every trained form of this idea that was tested missed its bar or broke a project rule. The plain exact store itself worked whenever its address was right. The form that matters most, where the address is the model's read, was never built. See what would reopen it.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

Write each fact once, under an exact address, and read it back exactly. Do not smear it across weights, and do not hunt for it by fuzzy similarity. The address is built from prime numbers: every word has its own prime, so the same words always name the same slot. A new value replaces the old one, but the old one stays recoverable. A fact that was never written can answer "I do not know". In the one probe that checked, the store was never the cause of a failure: among 1,905 held-out misses, none was an eviction or a wrong stored value. What failed was the model's learned step of forming the address from a question.

What it replaces in a transformer

The key-value memory. A transformer keeps a key and a value for every earlier word and finds the right one by comparing the question against all the keys. Here the question is turned into an address instead, and the address is looked up directly. No comparison against every key is needed.

Left, how a fact is written, corrected and read, with the two honest failure answers. Right, why the tested models failed: the store was fine, the address was not formed.

How it works

Three built forms share one idea. In each, the address is exact.

1. Exact log and prime sieve (measurement on fixtures; the gcd arithmetic itself is proof). Every user turn is logged as word atoms. Each word has a prime from a registry table. A clause's address is the product \(A_c=\prod_{p\in S_c}p\) over its set \(S_c\) of distinct content primes, plus its ordered pairs of neighbours (n-lets). A query \(q\) is built the same way. A clause is admitted when

\[\gcd(q, A_c) > 1,\]

that is, when they share at least one prime. The greatest common divisor is computed as a sorted merge of the two factor lists, so no division is needed. Ranking is a separate step: most shared primes first, then latest occurrence, then ordered-pair match. A record counts as evicted only when its ring slot was actually overwritten.

2. The exact relation store (AERM, "G v1"). Learned heads tag each token as entity, relation, value or other. An integer store maps (entity, relation) to a value. It also keeps the previous distinct value and a version counter. A read answers one of four ways for the current and the previous version: None, Hit, Absent or Evicted. A prime-route variant keys by the semiprime \(k=p_a p_b\) of two atoms. By unique factorization (proof), \(k\) names the unordered pair exactly. The value is routed through the expert so that direction survives.

3. Product-key memory. The query splits into two halves. Each half is scored against \(S\) sub-keys and the top \(k\) on each side are kept. That gives \(k^2\) candidate slots, scored by the sum \(s_1(i)+s_2(j)\). The best \(k\) slots are read from an \(S\times S\) table. With \(S=256\) the table has 65,536 rows and a token reads 32 of them. The sub-keys are learned, or fixed to the 120 unit icosians or the 240 E8 roots. The built form mixes the rows with softmax weights.

Reading these honestly. The pattern is consistent. Where the address was given or written by a fixed rule, the store worked: the 1.000 in distribution, the zero eviction failures, and the 106 of 109 recall. Where a learned head had to form the address from new phrasing, it failed, and the failures sit in the tagging, not the storage. The product-key runs tested something else: they replaced a feed-forward block with a table, not the read. The project's own correction note says so, so they do not test "address instead of search" at all. The recorded failures belong to configurations (a 1.4M-parameter probe with a learned trigger; 2,000-step fine-tunes of one 29M model on a 40-row panel with softmax weights). They do not close the mechanism (D22).

A caution on weight. Retrieval caused only 2.2 percent of the failing rows in the era-22 chat panel (issue #1708), so it is open whether memory is the binding constraint on the first milestone at all (hypothesis).

What has never been tested

  • A true gcd sieve on the integer path. As of 1 October only a pairwise membership scan had been built.
  • Same relation in different words, using a learned channel that feeds the exact channel, at the 0.9 relation-accuracy gate.
  • Ordered n-let keys for atoms that are not role-disjoint.
  • Eviction proofs driving "I do not know" at long context in a trained model.

What would reopen it

  1. Build the address as the read. Add memory fields to the dialogue settings and train the store and read in from the start, with 2 to 3 seeds and a frozen panel of at least 80 rows. The brief's bar is at least 8 more rows of 40 than the 19 of 40 seen, with bits per byte within 0.01.
  2. Run the serving-time oracle first. Supply the true slot address and measure the gain before any training.
  3. Re-register lawfully. Use an offline float sheet (D37) or a discrete sheet (D32) with a softmax-free value mix (a rank table or a hard select), a separately scanned module, an integer export and a reported export gap. This needs a fresh TEST FITNESS: FIT review and an owner release.
  4. Build an integer read kernel: gcd or sorted-merge admission plus a table value read, in the integer serving crate.
  5. Report address formation apart from read accuracy, since 77.7 percent of the held-out failures were query-entity tagging.

Related mechanisms

pointer-key: copies the value token the address names. The pointer found the source but not the slot. read-binding: teaches an attention read which stated value belongs to the question, the learned alternative to an exact address. object-store: exact byte storage of source material beneath the model, with no addressing of facts. e8-orbit-memory: the E8-addressed product-key variant, replacing a feed-forward block. relation-read: reads retained structure, where exact edges would come from this store. admission: the measured ceiling on what any read can reach. prime-zeta-codebook: supplies the prime registry the sieve depends on. route-read and flock-read: similarity-free alternatives that read by address or by a small kept set.

Exact byte object store

Status: READY. It is built and byte-tested: 60 object-store tests pass, and a second-language client reads from it correctly. No model uses it yet, and the durable-memory acceptance bars for milestone M3 (remembering across sessions; see the milestones) have not been run.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

This is storage, not thinking. It keeps data exactly, so a chat memory can be saved, checked and copied between machines without any byte changing. The data is cut into small pieces. Each piece is fingerprinted, and the pieces are arranged in a tree. Repeated content is stored once. Any byte range can be read back and checked on its own. When a file changes a little, only the changed pieces need to travel. It does not shrink new text; unique text takes about twice as much room. It exists so that a future model has something exact to quote from.

What it replaces in a transformer

Nothing. A transformer has no part like it. It sits beneath the model as durable memory outside it. The nearest transformer idea is a key-value cache that survives a restart, but this store holds raw source bytes with no keys, no facts and no addresses. Exact memory is the part that would address facts. Its node ids are content fingerprints and are never geometric addresses.

Left, a small read touches only a few verified nodes. Middle, an edit sends only the changed records. Right, repeats shrink and unique text grows.

How it works

Cutting and folding (proof of the format, measurement of the sizes). fold(bytes) splits the data into ordered 32-byte atoms. The last atom is zero-padded. A 32,768-byte object is therefore 1,024 atoms. The atoms become the leaves of a canonical ternary (three-child) tree of records.

A record holds a scale byte and a 12-byte fingerprint (BLAKE2b-96, a hash) of the scale and payload. After that comes either a 32-byte leaf or three ordered 12-byte child ids. A leaf record is 45 bytes and an internal record is 49. A child's scale must equal its parent's scale minus one, which forbids cycles. Equal chunks hash to the same record, so repeated content is stored once while every ordered occurrence is kept.

Manifest and version. A manifest pins the length, the ordered roots and a whole-object SHA-256. The object version is the SHA-256 of the canonical manifest. rebuild checks the padding and the whole-object SHA-256, so the byte obligation is

\[\mathrm{rebuild}(\mathrm{fold}(b)) = b\]

for every input \(b\) within the limits (a tested obligation, with 20 integration controls at delivery; not a machine-checked proof).

Range reads. range(start..end) descends only the branches that intersect the range. It authenticates each visited record against the root. A 23-byte read of a 32,768-byte object touched 2 leaves and needed 8 authenticated nodes, 384 serialized bytes. A missing, unrelated leaf did not block that range. It did block a full rebuild.

Token bindings. Occurrence bindings tie every token occurrence of a pinned tokenizer to an object version and a byte span. They are versioned separately from the object, so exact token, occurrence and version identity never merges with a geometric address. The adapter refuses lossy or normalised sources instead of guessing offsets.

Peers. A receiver asks only for node ids it is missing, verifies each digest, and commits all at once or not at all. The wire format is specified byte by byte in PROTOCOL.md.

What it does not do. Deduplication is not general compression. Unique 32,768-byte content takes 70,972 record bytes, which is \(70{,}972/32{,}768\approx 2.17\) times the raw size (measurement). Pins prove integrity, not who sent the data. No collision fixture was built for the 12-byte node id.

Rule check. There is no model, no learning and no geometry here. The source has no softmax, sigmoid or tanh (searched), no matrix multiplication and no floating point apart from a test timer. The hash primitives are integer. No instruction-level audit against the zero-multiplier serving rule (D11) has been run. It adds nothing to the discrete training path (D32).

What has never been tested

  • Any model reading from the store, whether exact quotation feeding the emitter or durable-session export and import. export_scope and import_scope are unchanged and unwired.
  • The third milestone's durable-memory bars on a chosen model: provenance, correction, "I do not know" for unstated or retracted facts, explicit reset, restart, and token-for-token identical restore.
  • A real wide-area measurement of pipelined fetch and of the verification pipeline.
  • A hostile network. Pins give integrity, not authentication.
  • Occurrence bindings against the real tokenizer at corpus scale.
  • Storage cost on real chat data against an ordinary compressor.

What would make it ACTIVE

  1. Name the first model consumer: exact quotation into the emitter, or durable-session persistence through the store.
  2. Pre-register the matching durable-memory bar and run it on a selected model.
  3. Decide where exact identity meets geometry. Exact token, occurrence and version identity must stay separate from geometric addresses.
  4. Decide who owns range reads: the store, or the separate reconstruction-tree reader, or one shared record backend.

Read binding (supervised value binding)

Status: PARKED. In the one form tested, it met its own target and moved the memory score by a pooled 8 of 120 rows over three seeds (one seed was down 1 row, and only one seed was individually significant). But it was applied to a softmax attention read, which the project now bans, and it has never been tried on any read that is allowed. It stays open.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

Ask a model "Ana's locker is 47. Ben's locker is 12. What is Ana's locker?" A common failure is to find a stated number but pick the wrong one. During training, a teacher marks which earlier words hold the value the question asks for, and which hold the other stated values. The model is rewarded when its attention lands on the right ones. Nothing changes when the model is used: the labels only shape what the attention learns. It aims at one failure, "found a value, but the wrong one".

What it replaces in a transformer

It adds to the loss, the training score. A transformer is usually trained only to predict the next word, and nothing tells its attention which earlier word to look at. This adds a second target on the attention read itself. It replaces no layer and adds no operation at serving time.

Left, attention before and after supervision. Right, the wrong-value count falls, and silencing the supervised layer removes the answers.

How it works

For a question whose next word belongs to a stated value, the training data carries two sets of earlier positions. \(B\) is the set that holds the asked value (bound). \(C\) is the set that holds the other stated values (competing). The labels come from a sidecar file written with the dialogue corpus. Each attention head \(h\) puts weight \(a^{(h)}_j\) on earlier position \(j\). Define the bound and competing mass:

\[m^{(h)}_{\text{bound}}=\sum_{j\in B}a^{(h)}_j,\qquad m^{(h)}_{\text{comp}}=\sum_{j\in C}a^{(h)}_j .\]

The extra loss, on the best-binding head, is

\[\mathcal{L}_{\text{bind}}=-\log\!\Big(\max_h m^{(h)}_{\text{bound}}+10^{-6}\Big),\qquad \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\text{language}}+W\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{bind}} .\]

The floor \(10^{-6}\) keeps the logarithm finite. The weight \(W\) was 0.1 in the run kept and 0.5 in the first test. The loss is zero only when all attention sits on the bound positions (ignoring the floor). That follows from the formula (proof). One variant also penalised competing mass with \(0.5\,\max(0,\,m_{\text{comp}}-0.03)\).

The labels never touch a hidden state or a score for the next word. The served network is unchanged, and only the read learns to separate values. The tested runs applied it to a late read layer (layer 8, in a stack whose reads are layers 2, 5 and 8) from step 0 of a fine-tune.

An exact-by-construction variant (read_lineage = phase_bind) gives each value a fixed phase tag, so binding is exact rather than learned. A random rotation tag is its control.

No matrix multiplication (D30)Not clean. The 29M-parameter stack that was trained is a dense matrix-multiplication stack

Discrete path (D32) and offline float (D37)Not on the discrete path. Float training is legal offline under D37, so the signal is admissible if attached to a lawful read and exported to an integer artifact

Reading these honestly. This is the clearest positive among the learned-read ideas, and also a narrow one. It was measured on a 40-row panel per seed, on fine-tunes of a single 29M-parameter model. The bound and competing masses are measured on training data. The headline gain is about 8 rows of 120.   • At least 120 memory rows per seed. Every panel has 40.
  • A model pretrained with the mechanism. Every run fine-tuned one 29M base.

  4. Change the supervision, not its length or sharpness. Per-head supervision, or routing the output through the binding head, are the named candidates.

Pointer copy with an exact identity key

Status: PARKED. Every tested form is a softmax pointer inside a dense float model, and each missed its bar or cannot be served. A real prime-based key raised the pointer's hit rate from 0.377 to 0.545, yet the answers did not reach the pre-registered bar (one seed got 23 of 40 memory rows against a bar of 25, inside the noise). The version keyed by the slot's own name was never run, nor was the forced-copy test of it on a lawful pointer.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

When asked "what is Ana's locker?", the model should copy the stored answer from earlier text rather than invent one. A pointer is a small part of the model that chooses which earlier word to copy. This mechanism wants the pointer to choose by the exact name of the slot (Ana plus locker), not by the surrounding wording. Measured on 9 October on 13 rows, the pointer instead lands on the repeated sentence frame ("... locker is ..."), and almost never on the changing digits.

What it replaces in a transformer

The copy head, also called an induction head. In a transformer, a head learns to look back at an earlier word and copy it. Here the choice of which word to copy is steered by prime-number addresses, so it does not depend on how similar two stretches of text look.

Left, where the pointer actually looks, and where the forced-copy test would put it. Right, a higher hit rate did not raise the memory score.

How it works

The copy mixture. The model's next-word distribution blends its ordinary scores with a copy distribution:

\[p(v)=(1-g)\,\mathrm{softmax}(z)_v+g\sum_{j:\,x_j=v}a_j ,\]

where \(g\) is a learned gate, \(x_j\) is the word at earlier position \(j\), and \(a_j\) is the pointer's attention over a window of earlier words. The first term uses a softmax, which matters for the rule check below.

The project-specific part is how a source is chosen.

  • Every word has a registered prime. A source \(j\) is admitted when the greatest common divisor of its atoms and the query's atoms exceeds 1: \[\gcd(q,\pi_j)>1 ,\] or when an ordered n-let (a short ordered run of atoms) matches. These are RouteAdmission::SharedAtom and Ngram.
  • Rarer atoms weigh more, by \(\ln\gcd\). The route score is scaled by 4.0 (ROUTE_SHARPNESS), and the attention is a softmax over admitted sources.
  • An identity term (PointerIdentity) adds the overlap of the six words before the source with the six before the query.
  • A fixed table folds upper and lower case and one leading space to a canonical id (copy_identity.rs). It only decides matches and never changes the emitted word.

The intended key is the slot address: entity prime times attribute prime, written when the fact is stated. Not the wording around the value. That version was never built.

Reading these honestly. The key did what a key should: it found the source more often, at no cost in likelihood. The answers did not follow. The record suggests why: the pointer branch carries only about 6 percent of the output mixture, and the answer-path test shows the answers come from the attention read. So the hit-rate measurements read a minor branch, and the bottleneck is after the source is found (hypothesis). The failures are specific. The identity runs keyed on the wrong thing. The gate run had a control that did as well. The v5 run had no memory operator at all. The inference knobs changed two decode settings on fixed weights. None of them tested a key on the slot's name, and the project's own rule says a negative closes a configuration, not a mechanism (D22).

What has never been tested

  • The forced-copy oracle: supply the true slot or span and see whether the answers follow. It has been named and left unrun since 12 October. It must not be run as a new execution of the softmax pointer artifact (D23, D30): it needs a lawful pointer, or stored outputs.
  • A pointer keyed on the slot's name (entity prime times attribute prime), as opposed to the six words around the value or a one-atom window.
  • Admitting a whole value span, such as the full two-digit run, instead of one token.
  • Exact admission with a learned ranking over addresses.
  • Any pointer on the discrete path, or with a copy distribution that has no softmax.
  • A pointer served as integers by gcd, with the export gap measured.
  • At least 3 seeds with at least 120 memory rows. Every pointer run was one fine-tune of one 29M model on a 40-row panel (the address-key test used three data orders).

What would reopen it

  1. Run the forced-copy oracle on a lawful pointer. Supply the true slot address or span to bound the possible gain, using a softmax-free, matmul-free pointer or stored outputs only. A new execution of the existing softmax pointer artifact is not allowed (D23, D30; see the mechanism board).
  2. Then train a slot-address key. A parsed or learned key (entity prime times attribute prime), trained in from the start of the dialogue fine-tune, with matched controls, at least 3 seeds and at least 120 memory rows. The bar is a gain of at least 5 rows of 40 over the control.
  3. Remove the softmax. Give the copy distribution a rank table, a hard select, or exact admission plus a learned ranking, so the head can be registered under the no-softmax and no-matrix-multiplication rules. That is a new offline float sheet (D37) or a discrete sheet (D32), with a fresh TEST FITNESS: FIT review and an owner release.
  4. Serve it as integers. Route by gcd or n-let equality with no float score, and report the export gap.

E8 orbit memory

Status: PARKED. Replacing half of the feed-forward layers with this memory stayed inside its quality bar (+0.033 bits per byte), but a learned address book of the same size beat the fixed E8 addresses by 0.023. So the geometry earned no credit. The read weight also uses a sigmoid, which the project now bans.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

Instead of running a full feed-forward layer, the model reads a handful of rows from a very large table. The row addresses come from the 240 special points of the E8 lattice, an eight-dimensional pattern of points (the E8 roots). A fast exact rule finds the nearest special point to each half of the query. The hope is a fixed, exact address book that touches a few rows per token rather than running a full dense layer. In the one trial, the fixed address book did slightly worse than an address book the model learns for itself.

What it replaces in a transformer

The feed-forward block (also called the MLP). In a transformer this is the large layer after attention that processes each word, and it holds most of the arithmetic. Here a table lookup of a few rows takes its place. The table is far larger, but only a few rows are read per token.

Left, how a query picks candidate rows. Right, the geometry stays inside the quality bar but behind its learned twin.

How it works

The E8 roots (the count is proof; the integer decode was checked by measurement on 20,000 queries). The 240 roots are 112 vectors of the form \((\pm1,\pm1,0,0,0,0,0,0)\) in any arrangement, plus 128 vectors \((\pm\tfrac12,\dots,\pm\tfrac12)\) with an even number of minus signs. The code stores them in doubled integer coordinates, so they are exact integers.

Per head, in four steps.

  1. Cut and decode. The query is cut into two 8-dimensional halves. Each half is decoded to its nearest E8 root in \(O(8)\) operations: the two largest \(|x_i|\) with sign rules, or all signs with a parity fix for the half-integer roots. No 240-way scan is needed. It was checked against a full scan on 20,000 queries.
  2. Orbits. SpiralCore's group of 64 signed axis permutations (\(\mathrm{Cl}(0,6)\)) splits the 240 roots into 15 orbits of 16 (240 = 15 × 16). A half's candidates are the 16 roots of its decoded root's orbit.
  3. Slots. The two halves together address a grid of \(240\times240=57{,}600\) value slots. The head keeps the top \(k\) by combined score (\(k=8\) in the rung that ran).
  4. Read. A kept slot of rank \(r\) is weighted by

\[w_r = R[h][r]\cdot\sigma(\beta s+\gamma),\]

a learned rank table \(R\) times a logistic-sigmoid gate on the score \(s\). There is no softmax. The output is the weighted sum of the kept value rows. Slot choice is detached from training, so only the query map, rank table, gate scale and the values learn.

Size. The value table has \(57{,}600\times256\) float values, about 59 MB per layer (proof by arithmetic: \(57{,}600\times256\times4\) bytes). A token reads 32 of its rows. The design arithmetic is about 27 thousand multiply-adds per token against 270 thousand for the dense layer it replaces, roughly tenfold. That figure is arithmetic, not a measured speed or energy saving.

Rule check.

RuleVerdict
No softmax (D23)Broken as built. The read weight uses a sigmoid, and sigmoid is banned along with softmax
No matrix multiplication (D30)Not clean. The query map and value mixing are dense float operations. The static E8 and SpiralCore tables were rebuilt without a generic 8 by 8 matrix product (record)
Integer-only serving (D11)No served form. Export refuses, and integer serving refuses product-key memory. The value tables are float. The decode, orbit tables and route transport are exact integer lookups
Discrete path (D32) and offline float (D37)Not on the discrete path. D37 would allow offline float training only as a new reviewed sheet with an integer export and a reported gap

Reading these honestly. The rung's decision rule was "half the layers within the larger of 0.05 or two times the noise", and E8h (+0.033) met it. That is why the outcome is keep-and-iterate, not a failure. But the learned twin beat E8h by 0.0231 BPB, about four times the noise. Learned sub-keys addressed the slots better than fixed E8 roots at this scale. The record could not tell whether the gap comes from the fixed addresses or from the value capacity per slot (hypothesis on either side). So the geometry earned no credit. Replacing all eight layers cost +0.116, which says too much capacity was removed at width 256 for 2,000 steps. It does not say E8 addressing fails. The result is one configuration: 2,000 steps, 2 seeds, a laptop CPU, a sigmoid gate. It was the last rung of its kind on the laptop CPU; geometric-stack training now goes to rented GPUs. The speed numbers are host-side slot selection, not an integer table read.

What has never been tested

  • Any E8 memory run after rung 1: no run with \(k=16\), no learned per-orbit offsets, no GPU run of the layer.
  • E8 memory trained in from pretraining. The rung trained a 256-wide stack for 2,000 steps from scratch on its own recipe.
  • A gate with no softmax and no sigmoid, or any discrete form of the layer.
  • Integer value tables and a served form, with measured tokens per second and an export gap.
  • E8 memory as the read itself ("address instead of search"). Only the feed-forward layer was replaced.
  • E8 as the write address of facts, with prime semiprimes as the exact check.
  • Query-level address quality. The entropy and coverage statistics are aggregates.

A fair test needs

From the earlier brief, archive/mechanisms/e8-orbit-memory-2026-10-20.md.

  • A capacity-matched learned-key control (P).
  • Routing health (entropy and slot share), to tell collapse from capacity.
  • Matched training steps and the same panel.
  • GPU training: a CPU run of E8a took about 6 h.

What would reopen it

  1. Run the next rung the record names, GPU only and pre-registered with a fresh TEST FITNESS: FIT review: raise \(k\) from 8 to 16, and add learned per-orbit residual offsets on the E8 frame. The offsets separate "fixed addresses" from "value capacity" as the cause of the 0.023 gap.
  2. Replace the sigmoid gate with one that obeys the no-softmax rule, such as a rank table with a hard threshold or exact selection. Register it as an offline float sheet (D37) in a separately scanned module with an integer export (integer value tables, E8 decode as table lookups) and a reported export gap. An owner release is required.
  3. Keep the fair-test conditions. A capacity-matched control (P, the learned-key twin, which uses a float sigmoid gate), taken from stored rung-1 outputs or replaced by a lawful count-table control because new neural controls are barred until the model works end to end (charter section 3.10); routing health (orbit entropy and slot share), matched training steps, the same panel, and at least 2 seeds.
  4. Provide a served form. Integer serving refuses product-key memory today, and a multiply-add saving did not appear in tokens per second for the learned-key twin. Report tokens per second.

Ternary and XOR/Hamming arithmetic

Status: PARKED. As proposed, a dense layer of −1/0/+1 weights removes the multiplier but not the sum over every weight, which the owner's no-dense-matrix-multiplication rule still counts against it. It was never trained in. Its two small pieces, bit counting and three-valued switches, already run inside the current model (discrete-learning).

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

A normal network stores each weight as a decimal number, and using it costs a multiplication. Here each weight is only −1, 0 or +1, so using it means add, subtract or skip. Two bit patterns are compared by counting how many bits differ, which is called the Hamming distance. The hope was cheap arithmetic with no multiplier. The plan to replace the big grids of multiplications this way has not been adopted, because every weight is still touched for every word and the owner's no-dense-matrix-multiplication rule counts that against it. The bit counting and the three-way switches are used in the current model.

What it replaces in a transformer

The arithmetic inside the big grids of multiplications (the matrix multiplications): the projections that turn each word's vector into queries, values and layer outputs.

The operators are AND and subtract, not XOR (left). Inside the current model, bit counting breaks ties between routes (middle). The multiplier goes away but the dense grid stays (right).

How it works

Storage (Definition). A ternary weight vector \(w\in\{-1,0,+1\}^n\) is stored in two bit planes. Plane \(P\) is set where \(w_i=+1\), plane \(N\) where \(w_i=-1\), and \(P\wedge N=0\). The repository's low-bit code uses two bits per weight (CODE_POS=1, CODE_NEG=2), which is the same thing.

The dot product is exact (proof). For a binary activation vector \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), \[\sum_i w_i x_i \;=\; \operatorname{popcount}(P\wedge x)-\operatorname{popcount}(N\wedge x).\] Each position contributes \(+1\) if and only if \(P_i=x_i=1\), and \(-1\) if and only if \(N_i=x_i=1\). A zero weight is skipped for free. For multi-bit activations \(x=\sum_b 2^b x^{(b)}\), repeat per bit plane and combine with shifts and adds. A power-of-two row scale is a shift. A 2026-10-12 re-check agreed in 5,000 random trials (measurement, owner-ruling record).

XOR is not the ternary dot product (proof). XOR gives the Hamming distance \(d(a,b)=\operatorname{popcount}(a\oplus b)=|a|+|b|-2|a\wedge b|\). Over the two-element field GF(2), \(-1\) and \(+1\) are the same element, so "ternary XOR matmul" is false as stated. What is true is the AND-and-subtract identity above.

What it does not remove (proof, by counting). A layer with \(D\) inputs and \(W\) outputs still reads all \(W\times D\) weights for every token. The multiplier disappears; the dense sum stays. A contraction applied only to a routed subset would not have this cost (hypothesis).

Where it runs today (Definition). In the discrete model the same ingredients serve as routing parts, in discrete.cu:

  • A coordinate Hamming count breaks ties when two candidate ports have equal L1 displacement for a transported query.
  • A ternary gate parameter switches flock levels on or off, with candidates visited in the order 0, −1, +1.

Geometry. On its own this is Boolean hypercube arithmetic, not a lattice. The E8 lattice is the (8,4,4) Hamming code lifted by Construction A, but Hamming distance on E8 labels is not the E8 lattice distance (decision D32).

Rule check.

  • D11 (integer serving): compatible in form, since add, subtract, skip and AND with popcount need no multiplier. Not shown to be fast: the one multiplier-free engine measured ran 68.0 tokens/s against 127.5 on the D10 engine (multiplies allowed) (record).
  • D23 (no softmax): nothing to scan; scoring is a hard count.
  • D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): the dense ternary sum is still a dense sum, so it would not pass as a matmul substitute. The tie-break and trit gates inside routing are not matmuls.
  • D32/D37: D32 names ternary and Hamming computation as a preferred substrate. D37 allows float training offline, but a ternary master would still need a new pre-registered sheet and an export gap (decisions).

Reading these honestly. The failures are failures of configurations: an unnormalised, ungated recurrence (the takeover review withdrew the broader reading); a quantiser applied after training to a float copy with a reduced search; one frozen-state refit; one engine on one laptop. None tests ternary weights trained from step 0 in a normalised or routed structure. The positive rows are authored finite tasks or toy recall, not language quality. The 4-bit rows use the same multiplier-free family but not the ternary alphabet.

What has never been tested

  • The actual XOR arm, with weight planes plus bit-sliced activations, separated from the weight-only arm.
  • A ternary alphabet of true group elements, such as the three cube roots of unity, instead of a truncated scalar.
  • A matched comparison against the icosian-mantissa weights (spin-weights) at equal steps, width and weight bytes.

A fair test needs

From the earlier brief, archive/mechanisms/ternary-xor-arithmetic-2026-10-20.md.

  • Mechanism trained in from step 0, not quantised post hoc. Every existing TernaryLinear use is a post-hoc snap of a float master; that arm is a reading, never a verdict.
  • A matched control at equal steps, width and weight bytes per token. For this project the honest control is quaternion_weights=all / icosian-mantissa, not an FP16 dense model — that is what already sits at parity and is already multiplier-free on the weight side.
  • ≥ 2 seeds with paired per-block analysis, or ≥ 200 fresh rows (D22). With existing noise of 0.0012–0.0027 BPB, the bar is ≥ 0.01 BPB or 2× measured noise, whichever is larger, fixed before compute, plus a stated tokens/s bar on the same harness.
  • Both operands declared, two arms: (i) weight planes only, activations multi-bit; (ii) weight planes plus bitsliced activations — the actual XOR arm. This separates the popcount cost from the ternary cost.
  • A qualified GPU kernel for the contraction before any language fit: exactness against forward_i32, device execution proven, host fallback refused.
  • Fresh transfer for any KEEP (D22), and a declared way to show the dense contraction left the executed path, including the training gradient (see open questions).
  • Uninterpretable if: the run trains on CPU (D24); arms differ in dtype, width, steps or tokeniser; the weight planes are rebuilt per token rather than per artifact; the popcount path is a forward-time wrapper while the trained graph keeps its dense contraction; or the comparison is a configuration D25 excludes.

What would reopen it

  1. A GPU kernel for the bit-sliced or table-lookup ternary contraction exists and matches TernaryLinear::forward_i32 for binary and 8-bit activations, with host fallback refused (decision D24: no model compute on the CPU).
  2. A pre-registered rung trains it in from step 0, against the matched icosian-mantissa arm at equal steps, width and weight bytes, with at least 2 seeds or 200 fresh rows. The bar is the larger of 0.01 bits per byte or twice the measured noise, set before compute.
  3. Tokens per second on the same CUDA harness goes up, not only multiplications or bytes touched. The integer engine lost 68.0 against 127.5, and product-key memory lost the same way, so this is the bar to beat.
  4. The contraction is applied where it is not a dense \(W\times D\) sum (a routed or selected subset), or the owner rules it an accepted, labelled non-geometric substitution, before any run.
  5. Or the alphabet is made geometric: three values that are actual group elements, such as the three cube roots of unity, instead of a truncated scalar quantiser.

Open questions: which operand is binary (today's activations are integer, so the XOR arm needs bit-plane activations); whether \(\{-1,0,+1\}\) fits the exact \(\mathbb Z[\varphi]\) objects; and, if ternary wins on cost and ties on quality, whether that is an accepted non-geometric substitution (an owner decision). These are hypotheses, not results.

Spin-native weights (quaternion and icosian maps)

Status: PARKED. The quaternion weights, snapped to a residual pair of icosians with a 2-bit scale, met their bar on a small test (1.5148 bits per byte: not distinguishable from a dense model with the same total parameters, and 0.107 behind a dense model of the same width; a single-icosian snap lost badly), but only by running a dense Hamilton-block multiplication, which the owner's rules ban. The code that ran them now refuses to run. The mechanism stays open.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

A network's weight matrix is usually a grid of independent numbers. Here each 4-by-4 block of the grid is replaced by one quaternion, a set of four numbers that describes a turn and a scale in four dimensions. That makes the grid four times smaller. After training, each quaternion is rounded to one of 120 exact rotations of the icosahedron (the 20-sided solid), plus a small scale. A product of two such rounded blocks then becomes a table lookup and a few shifts and adds, with no multiplication. The size and quality results were good. The speed benefit was never built or measured.

What it replaces in a transformer

The weight matrices of the projections: the grids that turn a word's vector into queries, keys, values, recurrence inputs and feed-forward layers.

Round a quaternion to the nearest of 120 rotations, then correct with a second small one; the product becomes a table read. The bars show what each step cost in quality.

How it works

Compact form (Definition). Each projection map is stored as an array \(Q[\text{out}/4,\ \text{in}/4,\ 4]\), one quaternion \((a,b,c,d)\) per 4×4 block, so there are four times fewer weights. A block acts as the Hamilton left-multiplication matrix \[L(a,b,c,d)=\begin{pmatrix}a&-b&-c&-d\\ b&a&-d&c\\ c&d&a&-b\\ d&-c&b&a\end{pmatrix}.\] The output quaternion is \(y_j=\sum_k Q_{jk}\otimes x_k\), with the input read as \(\text{in}/4\) quaternions. Each block costs 16 multiply-adds, so by itself the compact form saves weights, not arithmetic (measurement: width 256 uses the same 5,537,792 multiply-adds per token as the dense width-256 model).

Snap (Definition). Each trained quaternion becomes \[m\cdot 2^{e}\cdot\Big(g_1+\tfrac14\,g_2\Big),\] where \(g_1\) is the nearest of the 120 unit icosians (the binary icosahedral group, exact over \(\mathbb Z[\varphi]\)), \(g_2\) is the icosian nearest the leftover residual, \(m\in\{1,\,1.25,\,1.5,\,1.75\}\) is a 2-bit mantissa and \(e\) is a power of two. That is about 19 to 20 bits per block instead of 128 for four 32-bit floats. Activations can be snapped to the same set after training.

Table product (Definition, never built). The 120 icosians multiply by a fixed 120×120 table. The records describe a snapped product as a table read plus shifts and at most two adds. The group table itself was verified: all 14,400 products (120×120) matched in the 2026-09-20 prefix-recovery check (measurement, record). A kernel that serves exact-set by exact-set block products was never written.

Why one icosian is too coarse (measurement). The 120 directions sit about 15 degrees apart. Adding the residual icosian cut the mean angle error from 14.75 to 4.73 degrees, about 9 times less direction error energy.

Rule check.

  • D11 (integer serving): the weight side is multiplier-free by design. The activation side and the table kernel were never built, and export of quaternion-weight models is refused in the code.
  • D23 (no softmax): the mechanism has none; snaps pick the nearest point.
  • D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): fails as run. The forward expanded each map to a dense matrix and called a library matrix multiply, and the snap itself was a matmul against the 120 icosians. The fused Hamilton kernel (OP2) is a handwritten dense block contraction, which D25 does not accept as a replacement. Both execution paths now refuse. The ban retired the contraction; it was not retired by a negative result.
  • D32/D37: the historical form is float. D32 froze it and D37 lets it back only as a new offline float sheet with a fresh review (decisions).

What has been tried

All training rows below are small: width 256, a recurrence-heavy stack, 2,000 steps on a chat corpus, 2–3 seeds. The model around the weights still used softmax (the quaternion-weights and icosian-mantissa records both state "softmax at runtime: yes"), so these runs isolate the weight representation, not a lawful model. Scores are held-out bits per byte (BPB), lower is better.

A fair test needs

From the earlier brief, archive/mechanisms/spin-native-weights.md.

  • Equal total parameters and equal weight bytes per token against dense.
  • A panel that first shows it separates model sizes.
  • At least 2 seeds, with paired per-block noise.

  2. An explicit architecture decision for a Hamilton-block trunk. The 18 October architect audit says the active discrete model has no dense projections to replace, so this is a new architecture. "Spinor/quaternion adapters" are already listed as a conditional item, to be considered only at a measured ceiling.
  3. A soft-to-hard activation-snap schedule, blending \(\alpha\cdot\text{snap}+(1-\alpha)\,x\) with \(\alpha\) rising to 1, compared with the +0.0196 BPB post-hoc cost, before any negative on activation snapping counts.
  4. A served-form table kernel measured in tokens per second on the same CUDA harness, with weight bytes per token held equal to the dense control (8.55 MB against 8.62 MB in the rung-0 study).
  5. At least 2 seeds with paired per-block analysis (noise 0.0012 to 0.0041 BPB in these records) and fresh transfer for any KEEP.

Open questions: how much of the activation-snap cost is direction and how much is scale; whether to snap during training or build directly in served form; whether a finer exact group (the 600-cell plus a scale codebook, or the second E8 shell) is better; and whether the equal-weight-bytes gain survives at scale. These are hypotheses.

Hamilton rotation gate

Status: READY. The exact forward and backward passes, the GPU kernels and the trainer switch are built and tested. The gate has never been trained: no language run exists, and nothing has been compared with the gate it replaces.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run or test, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

Inside a feed-forward layer, a gate decides how much of a signal passes through. The usual gate squashes a number into the range 0 to 1 with a sigmoid curve, and the project's rules now ban that curve. This gate instead turns a gate signal into a rotation in four dimensions and rotates the matching value by it, four numbers at a time. A rotation only turns a vector. It uses no exponential and no squashing. A consequence worth knowing: a rotation cannot make a vector shorter, so this gate steers the signal rather than switching it off. Whether that is enough is not yet known.

What it replaces in a transformer

The gate in the feed-forward layer (the multilayer perceptron) that follows attention. The common form, SwiGLU, multiplies the value by a sigmoid-shaped gate.

What the swap does and does not do. The rotation keeps the signal's length; the length of the gate block enters only through the backward pass (right, drawn from the formula).

How it works

Work on blocks of four numbers. Let \(g\) be a gate block and \(u\) the matching "up" (value) block of the hidden layer. Compute \[r=\sqrt{|g|^2+10^{-12}},\qquad q=g/r,\qquad \text{out}=q\otimes u,\] where \(\otimes\) is the Hamilton product (the quaternion product) and \(q\otimes u=L(q)\,u\) with the \(4\times4\) matrix \(L\) given on the spin-weights page.

Two facts (proof).

  • Quaternion length is multiplicative, \(|q\otimes u|=|q|\,|u|\), and \(|q|=|g|/\sqrt{|g|^2+10^{-12}}\). So \(|{\rm out}|=|u|\) up to a factor that falls below 1 only when \(|g|\) is near \(10^{-6}\) or smaller (at \(|g|=10^{-6}\) the factor is \(0.71\)). A zero gate block gives \(q=0\) and zero output. The output's length is set by \(u\) alone; the gate sets only its direction.
  • The backward pass is exact, including the normalisation (Definition): \[\partial u=\bar q\otimes d,\qquad \partial q=d\otimes\bar u,\qquad \partial g=\frac{\partial q-q\,(q\cdot\partial q)}{r},\] with \(d\) the incoming adjoint and \(\bar q\) the quaternion conjugate. No exp, sigmoid, tanh or softmax appears in either direction.

The hazard (proof, from the formula). Because \(\partial g\) divides by \(r\), a gate block near zero gives a gradient of about \(1/r\approx10^{6}\). Weight decay can push a block toward zero. No real run has checked this.

Wiring. The hidden width must be divisible by 4. One GPU thread handles one block. The setting gate=hamilton selects it; the default stays the sigmoid SwiGLU gate so old artifacts load byte for byte. Export for integer serving and quantisation-aware training refuse any non-default gate. The same operation is also the output gate of the geometric recurrence.

What the owner's card left open (hypothesis). An icosian snap of \(q\), so the product becomes a read in the 120×120 table; an exact hard forward with a straight-through gradient bridge; and a serving form.

Rule check.

  • D11 (integer serving): not servable today. The exporter refuses other gates, and the normalisation divides by a square root and multiplies two runtime values. It becomes table-servable only after the icosian snap makes \(q\) one of 120 rotations.
  • D23 (no softmax or squashing): passes by construction. D25 closed the sigmoid exception that SwiGLU relied on, which this replaces.
  • D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): a per-block Hamilton product is not a dense contraction. The owner permits a geometric feed-forward block of this gate plus Hamilton-block projections, and the projection half has since been replaced by SpiralCore/FBS.
  • D32/D37: a float operation, frozen by D32. D37 lets it return only through a new pre-registered offline sheet (decisions).

Geometric recurrence gates

Status: READY. The clamped opening, the table of fade rates, the secant credit rule and the Hamilton output gate are built, and 18 finite controls (11 on CUDA, 7 metadata or argument checks) pass. The gates have never been trained, and the fit that was meant to test them never ran.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run or test, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

A recurrent layer keeps a running memory and decides at each step how fast old content fades and how much new input gets in. The old recipe used smooth curves for those decisions (sigmoid, exponential, tanh), and the project's rules now ban them. The replacement opens the input with a clamped straight line, picks the fade rate from a short table of powers of two, and carries the memory forward by a rotation. Each step is a table read and a rotation, so nothing smooth is needed. It is a drop-in for the gates of one particular recurrent design, not a standard part of a transformer.

What it replaces in a transformer

A plain transformer has no recurrence, so this replaces nothing there directly. It belongs to the recurrent alternative to attention used in the project's older float stack. In that design it replaces four squashing functions inside the recurrence: a sigmoid opening, an exponential and softplus decay rate, and a tanh-shaped output gate.

A table of 16 fixed clocks replaces a smooth dial. Each step multiplies the old state by the chosen rate and a rotation, and adds new input scaled by the matching keep factor.

How it works

The trunk's sequence mixer is a recurrence over lanes of four numbers (quaternions). From the source (geometric_stack.rs), one step per lane is \[h_t \;=\; \lambda_t\,u_t\otimes h_{t-1}\;+\;\kappa_t\,b_t,\] where \(u_t\) is a unit quaternion built from the gate projections (the rotation), \(b_t\) is the convolved input drive, and \(\otimes\) is the quaternion product. Four squashing sites of the historical form are replaced in the mode rec_gates=geometric:

  1. Opening (Definition). \(s_t=\mathrm{clamp}(g_t+d,\,0,\,1)\), where \(g_t\) is the gate projection and \(d\) is a per-lane decay parameter read raw, with no softplus. The clamp has an exact subgradient.
  2. Rate (Definition). The index is \(i=\min(\lfloor 16\,s_t\rfloor,\,15)\). The rate and the keep factor are read from two 16-entry tables: \[\lambda=2^{-(i+1)},\qquad \kappa=\sqrt{1-\lambda^2}.\] The rates are exact powers of two, from \(1/2\) down to \(2^{-16}\), and \(\kappa\) is precomputed beside each one, so serving needs only table reads. The pair \((\lambda,\kappa)\) lies on the unit circle up to \(6\times10^{-8}\) (measurement; the last four \(\kappa\) entries round to exactly 1 in 32-bit floats).
  3. Carry (unchanged). The quaternion scan above.
  4. Output gate (Definition). The Hamilton rotation gate on the recurrence output, replacing a tanh-shaped gate.

Credit through a hard choice (Definition). Picking a table entry has zero derivative almost everywhere, so nothing would train. The backward pass uses a declared secant surrogate: it pairs the incoming adjoints for \((\lambda,\kappa)\) with the full counterfactual change in the table between the selected entry and each neighbour, and resolves the contrast along the fixed edge of length \(1/16\), half to each side and the whole weight to the single neighbour at either end. No probability or exponential is involved. It is a rule, not the derivative of hard selection, and whether it yields descent is the open test.

A reading of the source (proof from the table, not a recorded finding). Every table entry satisfies \(\lambda\le\tfrac12\), so a step keeps at most half of the old state times a rotation. The historical rate \(\lambda=\exp(8\,\sigma(g)\log\sigma(d))\) can approach 1 as the opening goes to 0. Whether a table capped at one half per step keeps enough long memory is untested.

The mode refuses non-GPU devices, export and quantisation-aware training. The historical mode stays the default so old artifacts reproduce.

Rule check.

  • D11 (integer serving): designed for it, since the rates are table reads, the opening is a clamp and the scan is rotations. Not yet exportable, because the integer engine binds the historical decay parameter. The output gate still needs the icosian snap.
  • D23 (no softmax or squashing): a grep on 13 October found 0 squash-family tokens in the geometric arms (the historical branches keep 8 by design).
  • D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): a clamp, a table read, a scan and a per-block rotation. The no-matmul and no-softmax counters were unchanged by the delivering PR.
  • D32/D37: a float operator. D32 froze it and D37 allows it back only by a new offline sheet (decisions). The active discrete model carries no recurrent state, so this belongs to a separate float trunk.

SpiralCore transport with ternary tree binders (float projection form)

Status: READY. The float projection is built and was checked on a real GPU with exact test cases, and it ran inside 18 finite controls. It has never been trained, and whether its credit rule gives descent is unmeasured. Its integer form is ACTIVE: it is the core of the current model, described under discrete-learning.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run or test, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

A normal layer mixes every input into every output using learned weights. This one does something much simpler. Each output block picks one input block from a small tree of stored blocks, three branches per node, and moves it along a path of exact steps in an eight-dimensional lattice called E8. Each step only swaps coordinates and flips signs. No learned coefficient is multiplied in; the path itself does the transforming. The trade is that each output reads one input block instead of a blend of all of them, and nobody has yet measured whether that carries enough information.

What it replaces in a transformer

The dense projections: the large weight grids that turn each vector into queries, values and layer outputs. In the float stack this replaced a dense quaternion version of the same job (spin-weights).

One output block, one chosen atom, a short path of signed coordinate swaps (left and middle). The dense projection connects every pair; this one connects one (right).

How it works

The tree (Definition). Input channels are 8-dimensional integer atoms kept by a static Rust compiler in ordered base-3 binders. The compiler stores children, parent links, atom identity, support length and the incomplete frontier (at most 6,560 atoms, 16 frontier roots and 8 stages). FBS is the project's name for this tree. Exact atom identity stays separate from the geometric state.

The steps (Definition, from SpiralCore). SpiralCore is an external exact-geometry source (a hosted file, reviewed on 9 October). Octonion left actions give 15 generators \(B\), each a signed coordinate permutation of \(\mathbb R^8\) with \(B^2=-I\). They act on the 16 roots of one E8 anchor orbit through 64 signed operator states. A breadth-first search over these labelled edges gives an ordered history between any two roots, composed by left-composition.

Exact inverse (proof). From \(B^2=-I\) it follows \(B^4=I\) and so \(B^3=B^{-1}\). The inverse of a history is therefore the reversed sequence with each step cubed.

Forward pass (Definition). The model stores query points \(z\in\mathbb R^{[\text{output blocks},\ \text{stages},\ 8]}\). At each stage a query picks the nearest root of the fixed orbit, and the history between roots composes a signed action \(A_j\). Output block \(j\) selects one atom \(\sigma(j)\) and transports it: \[y_j \;=\; A_j\,x_{\sigma(j)} .\] The forward is a gather and a sign. The input adjoint is the exact inverse action, \(A_j^{-1}\delta_j\), scattered to the selected atom. No coefficient exists for any input-output pair (proof, by construction).

Credit for the query (Definition). Selecting a root is a hard choice. The query credit is a declared secant surrogate on root edges: force each lawful sibling, reroute its descendants, pair the output credit with the displacement of the carried block, and resolve along the edge. It is not the derivative of hard selection.

The capacity question (proof of the count, hypothesis of the consequence). Each output block reads exactly one input atom, so an output block has one connection where a dense projection has all of them. Whether one transported atom per block is enough, or whether a small routed set per block is needed, has not been compared.

The path runs on the GPU only; the CPU fallback is refused.

Rule check.

  • D11 (integer serving): the float form (32-bit and half-precision) is not servable. Sign flips, permutations and table reads need no multiplier, and the integer descendant in crates/uor-r4-discrete is integer-only on the GPU.
  • D23 (no softmax): no probability weights, no normalised exponentials and no learned input-output coefficient grids; selection is hard by distance. The no-softmax counter was 1649 of 1649 on the delivering PR.
  • D25/D30 (no dense matrix multiplication): retires the dense Hamilton contraction. The no-matmul counter fell from 95 to 93. Static table construction reads no model tensors and is not model compute.
  • D32/D37: the float form was frozen by D32 and can return only by re-registration under D37. The integer transport is the substrate D32 names as the backbone, and it is the ACTIVE model path (decisions).

What has never been tested

  • Training the float projection. Zero optimizer updates have run on it, and no language measure exists.
  • Whether the secant credit yields descent. The pair credit is declared, not proved.
  • Capacity of one atom per block against an all-input mixing projection. No capacity or cost comparison was run.
  • Input-conditioned behaviour. Selection by shared learned queries does not by itself make the read depend on the input.
  • Coverage of all 240 E8 roots. Only one 16-root anchor orbit is used, with no independent partner space and not the complete external tree object.
  • Tokens per second or energy against the retired dense arm, and any integer export of the float form.

What would reopen it

The float form is READY, so these are the steps to make it ACTIVE.

  1. A new D37 sheet in a separately scanned float module, with a fresh test-fitness review, the owner release that applies, an export gap, and the shared writer and geometric head as dependencies.
  2. Show that the secant credit gives descent (a falling loss, or a comparison with a random-refit control) and that routing is stable. Neither has been measured.
  3. Justify the total number of 8-dimensional blocks in advance, and record that each output block reads one atom, so a capacity comparison against a mixing projection is needed.
  4. Fresh transfer and D22 noise requirements for any KEEP, and tokens per second on the same GPU harness against the retired dense arm.

Open questions: does one atom per output block lose too much against the all-pair sum, and can a small routed set per block recover it; can the secant credit be compared with the discrete counterfactual-and-choose rule on the same carrier; how many 8D blocks are enough (the 6,560-atom bound is operational, not a quality bar, and no 384-dimensional dependency is adopted); and would a float trunk add anything beyond the integer path that already runs. These are hypotheses.

Geometric stack (layered quaternion-recurrence language model)

Status: PARKED. The version that was trained leaned on arithmetic the project later banned (softmax reads, sigmoid and SiLU gates, dense matrix products), and it never met the first milestone's bars. Its quaternion "spinner" idea was kept. A rules-compliant rebuild exists only as a small, untrained extract. See what would reopen it.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

This was the project's main trained language model from late September to mid-October 2026, between 7 and 214 million parameters. It reads text through a stack of layers. Most layers carry a running memory made of four numbers, a "spinner" called a quaternion. At every word the spinner is turned a little and the old memory fades. A few layers look back over earlier words, and every layer ends in a small feed-forward block. It was trained on GPUs, then rounded to whole numbers so a laptop could run it. It produced chat-style replies, though only 43 of 232 reply checks passed and it was served through the integer engine on pod CPUs. It used arithmetic the project later banned, and it never reached its quality bars.

What it replaces in a transformer

The whole network. The recurrence layers do the job that attention does in a transformer, carrying context forward. The read layers and feed-forward blocks, though, are the transformer's own parts. The project's own audit in October found that the served model was a transformer-shaped dense stack with a quaternion-mixed residual. The geometry was a thin layer inside it (see the figure).

Left, where one token's arithmetic went in the 29-million-parameter stack. Middle, what one recurrence lane does. Right, which parts of the trained form the later rules allow.

Its chapter in the project's history

  • 26 to 30 August (planning a decoder). Before building a stack, the project checked whether ordinary attention could live inside the geometry. A rotation-frame version of softmax attention matched a donor model's logits to within 1.05e-5, but it carried no meaning of its own. Trace distillation added nothing (#1002, #1011).
  • 30 August. A 7.16-million-parameter softmax language model in R4/Spin frames showed learned attention matters: loss per token 2.1274 with it, 4.8048 without. A single frozen continuation to 150 million tokens ended at 1.5728, short of its 1.50 bar (#1014, #1017).
  • 25 September. A 1.68-million-parameter recurrent learner with quaternion transport lost narrowly to a matched ordinary one (2.110 against 2.085) (#1389).
  • 27 to 29 September. A capacity-matched layered stack reached parity with a transformer control, and the owner made multiplier-free serving the one contract for every lab (D11, #1437, #1443). The stack became the main line.
  • 6 to 10 October. The first chat stack was trained, exported and served end to end (#1893). Matching the training data mattered more than adding parameters (#1913). Memory and reply targets were missed.
  • 11 October. An arithmetic audit showed the quaternion rotations were 0.05 percent of the arithmetic (#2186).
  • 12 to 13 October. The bans on softmax, matrix multiplication and squashing functions arrived (D23, D25, D29, D30). Thirty-three kernels carrying banned content were moved out of every compiled module, and a 24-kernel lawful extract was kept. The discrete path (crates/uor-r4-discrete) then became the live model.

How it works

Layer pattern (definition). Layers repeat in a pattern such as rrarra. Each r is a recurrence layer and each a a read layer. Every layer is followed by a feed-forward block, inside a residual stream with RMS normalisation.

Recurrence (definition). Lanes of four channels hold a quaternion state \(h_t\). Per token,

\[h_t = \lambda_t\,(u_t \otimes h_{t-1}) + \sqrt{1-\lambda_t^{2}}\;c_t ,\]

where \(\otimes\) is the Hamilton product, \(u_t\) is a unit quaternion computed from the input (it starts at the identity), \(\lambda_t\) is a gated decay with timescales spread from 2 to about 1,000 tokens, and \(c_t\) is a width-4 causal convolution of the input. Multiplying by a unit quaternion is a rotation of 4-space, so \(u_t\) turns the memory without changing its length.

Reads and feed-forward. Read layers attend over earlier positions with a dot-product, Euclidean or Lorentz hyperbolic-distance score. Feed-forward blocks are SwiGLU with dense projections. Optional parts were a copy-pointer head, a product-key memory that replaced a feed-forward block or the last read, and flock or starling rank reads.

Training and serving. Trained in float on GPU at 7M, 19.9M, 29M and 214M parameters, then exported to 4-bit grouped weights and served by the integer engine described in lut-serving.

Where the arithmetic went (measurement, an operation count of the deployed 29M stack, width 576, 10 layers). Of 30,270,720 multiply-adds per token, the feed-forward blocks took 39.6 percent, recurrence projections 31.0 percent, reads 16.6 percent (40.5 percent at 4,096 tokens of context) and the output head 7.4 percent. The quaternion rotations took 16,128 multiplies, or 0.05 percent. The prime addresses, zeta phases and exact store took none, because they were not in the trained base (geometry audit).

Reading these honestly. The stack reached parity with a transformer control at small scale, and it was served bit-for-bit through an integer engine. The quaternion transport kept its place in the core on a development measurement. But the pieces that did the work were dense ones, the recurrence was never shown to help in a model built from allowed parts, and no run met the memory or quality bars. A loss win was not a conversation.

What has never been tested

  • A stack built only from allowed parts (Hamilton-gate feed-forward, power-of-two recurrence, rank or flock reads), trained at the scale where this one reached 0.877 bits per byte. The 24-kernel extract is qualified at small finite checks only.
  • Product-key memory layers with fixed H4 and E8 codebooks (cycle 5; held, never run).
  • Trained-in icosian or E8 read addresses with their length carried.
  • The Lorentz read at chat scale. The chat base trained with the flat Euclidean read.
  • A larger chat data set than the 82-million-token split (none was reachable).
  • A fair energy measurement. The only figures come from a truncated capture and a table-emulation test that cost 4.3 times more.
  • A step-matched control for the 22 of 40 reading that the half-length memory run produced.

What would reopen it

  1. A new pre-registered sheet that rebuilds the stack from allowed parts only, in its own scanned module, with the owner's release (D37). It needs a TEST FITNESS: FIT review first.
  2. Report the export gap on the same evaluator as the float score, and aim at the served bar (at most 0.90 bits per byte on the chat held-out stream).
  3. At least 2 seeds or 200 fresh rows (D22), compared only with earlier native rungs and count-table references (D28).
  4. Replace the dense hotspots (feed-forward 39.6%, recurrence projections 31.0%) with addressed or exact-geometry reads, and show that tokens per second move on the product path.
  5. Optional: the quaternion adapter in the post-dose plan (optimization path), conditional and measured against the ceiling.

R4G1 compiled lookup graph (teacher-to-tables)

Status: PARKED. Its gains were measured while the teacher's own text was supplied, and they never turned into coherent text the model wrote itself. Building the tables also needs a transformer teacher, which the project now bans. The packed file format and the frozen run-time program stay as a tested, multiplier-free reference. The owner decided on 19 October 2026 to repair the legacy crates around this mechanism so they build again; that restores the build, not the mechanism. See what would reopen it.

Labels used below: proof means derived from definitions or code, measurement means a recorded run, hypothesis means an untested idea. See docs/formal_vocabulary.md.

In plain words

This was the project's first approach, from June to August 2026. Let an ordinary language model, the "teacher", read a lot of text. Record what it prefers in each situation and store those preferences as huge lookup tables. To answer, a small program finds the matching table row and picks the best next word using only whole-number adds and comparisons, with no multiplying. On a held-out set of 72,130 positions its table choice agreed with the target word 29.52% of the time, against 28.12% for the earlier runtime. It never wrote coherent text on its own, and building the tables needs a transformer teacher, which the project now forbids. The file format and the run-time program are kept as a tested reference.

What it replaces in a transformer

The whole engine, at run time. Instead of running attention and feed-forward layers, the program hashes the last few words into a table address and adds up stored scores. The price is that the knowledge is copied from a transformer, so the lookup tables can be no better than what the teacher showed them.

Left, how a teacher becomes a table and how a token is read from it. Middle, the main held-out result and its controls. Right, more text kept helping with no knee.

Its chapter in the project's history

This was Phase A of the project, from 10 June to 26 August 2026 (eras 1 to 10 of the project history). Dates below are the days issues or pull requests were opened.

  • June to July. The first code was a router over sparse 512-dimension prime vectors (#1). The R4G1 file format, certificates and the rule that only serving must be multiply-free and allocation-free followed (#11, #157). This stretch was mostly structure.
  • 23 July to 3 August. The first quality chain started at 0.3 percent accuracy against a 31.7 percent baseline (#65). A metric that read zero had hidden a real loss (#102). A store built with shift-and-add arithmetic and zero multiplies matched and slightly beat a larger earlier one (#243).
  • 3 to 12 August. Geometry was tried as an index. E8 codebooks beat plain sign codes at equal bits (#395). Hopf projection and the zeta-grid routing headline failed (#430, #440). SmolLM2-360M became the pinned teacher (#509).
  • 10 to 19 August. Recompilation and serving. A record-ordering bug turned out to be a major cause of garbage output (#755).
  • 19 to 26 August. A staged plan (S0 to S7) set a truth baseline of 29.52 percent against 28.12 percent (#821). Calibrated abstention, free-running text and planning all ended at their stated limit, and one lane was inert (#946). On 25 to 26 August the maintainers reset the plan: coherent free-running generation had never been shown, so a learned geometric decoder became the goal (#948, #949).
  • Afterwards. The no-multiply rule became the serving contract for the whole project (D11, see lut-serving). Later decisions retired the float and softmax parts of the old compiler from the core, so the graph crates stopped building against it (D36).

How it works

Offline (compile). A teacher transformer (SmolLM2 or GPT-2) runs over a corpus and its preferences are recorded. A compiler packs them into an R4G1 graph, a content-addressed file holding:

  • records keyed by hashed context codes (recent-token n-grams and prefix regions);
  • a cover of regions induced by entropy-gain splits;
  • pre-rounded integer score tables for each region;
  • optional extra lanes (skip-mix candidate injection, segment, trajectory);
  • certificates comparing the graph with the teacher on held-out positions.

Compilation, certification and every teacher run are offline and unrestricted.

Online (run). To pick the next token the program:

  1. hashes the recent tokens into a context code;
  2. takes the exact-context record, or the best-matching region (nearest match over compact bit signatures by counting differing bits, scored with a shift-and-add dot product in place of a multiply);
  3. adds each evidence source's stored integer scores, each counted once, saturating at the limits;
  4. breaks ties by a fixed rule and emits the best token.

In symbols (definition), with \(E\) the set of evidence sources found and \(r_e[t]\) the stored score of token \(t\) from source \(e\) in fixed-point arithmetic (\(v\) is stored as the integer nearest to \(v\cdot 2^{16}\)):

\[S(t)=\operatorname{sat}\Big(\sum_{e\in E} r_e[t]\Big),\qquad \hat t=\arg\max_t S(t).\]

The frozen kernel contract permits only XOR, AND, OR, shifts, rotates, bit counting, integer add and subtract, comparisons and table reads. There is no float, multiply, divide or allocation after setup (inference contract).

Geometry tried inside this frame. Prime and zeta-phase routing keys, Hopf S3-to-S2 observation, E8 and 120-root codebooks, H4/icosian frames, max-plus route composition and Furey algebra modules. Only the E8 codebook (better than sign codes at matched bits) and the integer shift-and-add dot product kept measured value. The rest tied or lost, and the Furey modules were never wired into inference.

Rule check.

No softmax (D23)Run-time scoring is softmax-free by contract. The offline path used the teacher's probabilities, and the retired compiler and runtime modules carry float and softmax content that may not be restored
No matrix multiplication (D30)The frozen runtime has none. Compiling needs a transformer forward pass, which is banned anywhere, and no transformer teacher or comparator is allowed (D28)
Offline float (D37)Float compiling would be legal in principle, but the teacher is separately banned. Nothing here is on the discrete GPU path, and the graph crates no longer build against the current core

What has never been tested

  • A graph compiled from a non-transformer source, such as exact tables read out of the native discrete model.
  • Free-running coherence of any compiled bundle. The correction rounds were never launched.

What would reopen it

  1. Decided on 19 October 2026. The owner chose to repair, not archive, graph-compiler, graph-certify, api, proof-model and the root crate on the current core (charter, section 2). Repair restores the build only; this mechanism stays PARKED.
  2. A compile source that is not a banned transformer teacher, such as tables read out of the native discrete model. The one-time donor corpus of D41 gives hard targets for training only, and not for graph compiling unless a new decision says so.
  3. A fresh pre-registration with a TEST FITNESS: FIT review, at least two seeds, scored against count-table references on free-running generation, not on teacher-forced agreement (D22, D28).
  4. Adoption of the packed container and frozen kernel as the export container for the served model (milestone M4), with the export gap reported (D37).
  5. Any added lane must change served tokens at deployed reachability. The trajectory lane changed none.
